• Fails if: surface won't mesh; gates exceeded (non-ortho 70°, skew 4); or the force never settles.
• You asked for turbulence model: the standing setup already runs it. • A different closure would need saying before solving, not after.
• The gates are the standard acceptance band, per OpenFOAM mesh-quality guidance. • The mesh is judged against a published threshold, not itself.

payload.message: • Surface measured: 712 triangles, streamwise X, span Y. • Working scale: 1.0 m long, 3.0 m across.
• Scale basis: the file's units are dimensionally plausible, so I am taking them as metres. • Wrong length → wrong Reynolds → wrong forces; stated, not buried.
• Case built: farfield from the body's own bounding box, k-omega SST. • Reference area: measured planform 3 m². • Freestream 15 m/s; Re 1.0e+06.
• Reference area is the measured silhouette, not a handbook wing area. • Book comparison needs rebasing first: measure the body, don't borrow numbers.
• Surface accepted: NACA 4412 finite wing, closed. • No defects reported by the surface check.
• Selected: k-omega SST, steady RANS, standard closure for attached external flow, solved on a quality-gated mesh.

payload.message: Conclusion
• Confirmed: raw surface → converged force in 2.6 min, no intervention. • Coefficient history flat over the window: the envelope means something.

• Confirmed against experiment: inside the published band of Abbott & von Doenhoff, Theory of Wing Sections (1959), NACA 4412 section data (section Cd ~ 0.006-0.009). • Validated, not merely converged: within 37% of Abbott & von Doenhoff, Theory of Wing Sections (1959), NACA 4412 section data (section Cd ~ 0.006-0.009), Cd 0.03 (band ±40%).
• Still unknown: mesh sensitivity, one mesh cannot separate discretization from physics. • A refinement study would roughly double the 2 core-minutes spent.

payload.title: Geometry study: NACA 4412 finite wing
abstract: We took NACA 4412 finite wing through surface check, meshing, and a steady solve to establish whether the chain yields a trustworthy force.
The mesh reached 337,334 cells at max non-orthogonality 49.9° and max skewness 3.32; drag settled at 0.01892 ± 1.9e-05.
The result is reported as validated: within 37% of Abbott & von Doenhoff, Theory of Wing Sections (1959), NACA 4412 section data (section Cd ~ 0.006-0.009), Cd 0.03 (band ±40%).
methods: Surface intake and check on NACA 4412 finite wing.
Background mesh plus snappyHexMesh to 337,334 cells; quality gated at 70° non-orthogonality and 4 skewness.
Potential-flow initialisation followed by 300 steady iterations.
Forces averaged over the final fifth of the iteration history; the band is the spread of that window.
